"""Approximate a local compound/modifier-completion feature.

Recognize dictionary compounds and some productive modifier families (duration,
scale, level, side, measurements, ownership). Handle possessives, numerical
endings, a few Chinese modifier families, and text starts separately. This is
not an arbitrary bigram lookup: families share one weight across their members.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet

READS = ()
FUNCTION = set("""a an the of to for in on at by as from with and or but if then
than this that these those there here it he she they we you i his her our your
their is are was were be been being am can could may might shall should will would
must do does did has have had not no so each every all any some such more less most
many much few""".split())
PARTICLES = set('in on off up out over down'.split())
PARTICIPLES = set(('driven derived defined made mounted owned held '
                   'born known shaped sized').split())
ORDINALS = set(('first second third fourth fifth sixth seventh eighth '
                'ninth tenth eleventh twelfth').split())

# Label, preceding words, final words, and additive contribution.
FAMILIES = (
    ('duration', 'long short longer shorter medium near mid',
     'term range distance run', 2.759),
    ('time commitment', 'full part real', 'time', 0.9143),
    ('scale', 'large small full wide broad medium macro micro gray grey',
     'scale', 3.9861),
    ('duty', 'heavy light', 'duty', 3.7267),
    ('side', 'front back left right server client upper lower', 'side end hand', 1.3337),
    ('level', 'high low higher lower top system district', 'level', 1.9273),
    ('sector', 'public private', 'sector', 3.3291),
    ('steady state', 'steady', 'state', 2.4027),
    ('newness', 'newly', '*', 0.4798),
    ('measurement', 'molecular high low higher lower constant variable',
     'weight frequency density speed precision definition energy '
     'voltage temperature pressure quality', 1.2093),
    ('real-world', 'real', 'life world', 1.6377),
    ('ownership/access', 'private public privately publicly',
     'held owned available', 2.296),
    ('openness', 'open closed', 'source form loop system', 1.8423),
    ('case', 'best worst upper lower edge corner', 'case', 1.0191),
    ('numeric format', 'fixed floating single double half', 'point precision', 0.683),
    ('extreme scenario', 'best worst', 'case', 2.4117),
)
FAMILIES = [(set(left.split()), set(right.split()), weight)
            for label, left, right, weight in FAMILIES]

@lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def pos(word):
    return wordnet.parts_of_speech(word)

@lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def pair_pos(p, q):
    return pos(p+'-'+q) | pos(p+' '+q)

@lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def command(p, q):
    return wordnet.is_a(p+' '+q, 'command') or wordnet.is_a(p+'-'+q, 'command')

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    start = carry is None or carry[0] != doc or carry[2]
    oldtext = '' if start else carry[1]
    text = oldtext+s
    carry = (doc, text[-80:], s == '<|endoftext|>')
    v = 0.002
    if start:
        return carry, (v + 0.376 - 0.1322*s.startswith(' ')
                       + 0.2346*s.strip().isalpha() + 1.7243*(s=='\t'))

    old = re.search(r'[A-Za-z]+$', oldtext)
    old = old.group().lower() if old else ''
    if s in {"'s", '’s'}:
        v += 0.4452
        if old in {'it','he','she','that','there','here','what','who','where','how','let'}:
            v -= 0.4205
    if s in {"'", '’'} and old.endswith('s'): v += 0.7668
    if oldtext[-1:].isdigit():
        if s.lower() in {'st','nd','rd','th'}: v += 1.0289
        if s in {'D','d'}: v += 0.4896

    # Compound words split inside a word, such as stand + alone.
    if (s.isascii() and s.isalpha() and len(s)>=3 and len(old)>=3
            and old not in FUNCTION):
        q = s.lower()
        if pos(old) and pos(q) and (pair_pos(old,q) or pos(old+q)):
            v += 0.1341
    if re.search(r'(?i)\b(nano|micro|meso|macro|milli|centi|kilo)scale$', text):
        if re.search('[A-Za-z]$',s): v += 2.8236
    for endings, weight in (
        (('大尺度','小尺度','大规模','小规模','大規模','小規模'), 2.0366),
        (('狭义','广义','狹義','廣義'), 2.653),
        (('大型','小型','中型','轻型','重型','輕型'), 0.1052),
        (('私有','公有'), 1.7525)):
        if text.endswith(endings): v += weight

    hyphen = bool(re.match(r'^-[A-Za-z]',s))
    if hyphen: v += 0.0931
    pair = re.search(r'([A-Za-z]+)[\s-]+([A-Za-z]+)$',text)
    if not pair or not re.search('[A-Za-z]$',s): return carry, float(v)
    p,q = (word.lower() for word in pair.groups())
    if hyphen and 'adjective' in pos(p+'-'+q): v += 0.2958
    content = p not in FUNCTION and (q not in FUNCTION or q in PARTICLES)
    if content:
        kinds = pair_pos(p,q)
        if 'adjective' in kinds: v += 0.426
        if 'noun' in kinds:
            v += 0.1615
            if command(p,q): v += 1.315
        if hyphen and pos(p) and pos(q): v += 0.1306
        if q=='based': v += 0.9014
        if q=='related': v += 0.4614
        if q in PARTICIPLES: v += 0.2919
    for left,right,weight in FAMILIES:
        if p in left and (q in right or '*' in right): v += weight
    ordinal = p in ORDINALS or p.endswith(('teenth','tieth')) or bool(
        re.search(r'\d\s*(?:st|nd|rd|th)[ -]+'+q+r'$', text, re.I))
    if ordinal:
        if q=='century': v += 1.0732
        if q in {'order','person','party','grade'}: v += 1.9233
    if p in FUNCTION:
        words = re.findall('[A-Za-z]+', text.lower())
        if any('adjective' in pos('-'.join(words[-n:]))
               for n in (3,4) if len(words)>=n): v += 0.8732
    return carry, float(v)

"""Recognize a small collection of conventional text completions.

Large negative pulses mark familiar URL, generated-code, forum and legal
boilerplate fragments. A few URL completions have positive pulses instead.
Each rule names the text immediately before a token, that token's text,
and its activation estimate. Ordinary text gets zero; boolean words and
tool delimiters get small offsets. This is only a partial lexical account,
not a general test for whether text is boilerplate.
"""
import re

READS = ()

# (preceding text, completing token, activation)
COMPLETIONS = (
    # Image hosting, badges and social-media links.
    ('user-images', '.githubusercontent', -9.5),
    ('cloud.githubusercontent.com', '/assets', -9.5),
    ('img.sh', 'ields', -6.5),
    ('img.shields', '.io', -4.75),
    ('shields.io/b', 'adge', -20.0),
    ('/#narrow', '/stream', -9.4),  # Zulip chat deep links
    ('cloud.mail.ru', '/public', -2.8),
    ('.slides', 'hare', -5.0),
    ('pbs', '.twimg', -3.9),
    ('groups', '.google', -7.7),
    ('sites', '.google', -4.9),
    ('code', '.google', -2.1),
    ('plus', '.google', -2.1),
    ('itunes', '.apple', -6.8),
    ('', '.twitter', -3.75),
    ('.youtube', '.com', -0.35),
    ('.wikipedia', '.org', 1.1),
    ('.apache', '.org', -0.55),
    ('/watch', '?v', 2.8),
    # Source generators, documentation, and familiar API constructs.
    ('jhipster-', 'needle', -5.5),
    ('begin-user', '-doc', -1.0),
    ('end-user', '-doc', -1.0),
    ('{@', 'link', -0.95),
    ('@', 'param', -0.47),
    ('</', 'param', -0.7),
    ('<', 'param', -0.5),
    ('store', '_true', -4.1),
    ('store', '_false', -6.0),
    ('sort', '.Slice', -1.7),
    ('Symbol', '.iterator', -1.1),
    ('', '.createSequentialGroup', -2.1),
    ('$.', 'ajax', -2.7),
    ('[/', 'QUOTE', -2.0),
    ('<a', ' name', -0.9),
    # Forum metadata, booking listings, and legal headings.
    ('\n-', ' TripAdvisor', -4.8),
    ('Latest', ' reply', -3.4),
    ('Latest reply', ' on', -1.6),
    ('K', 'udos', -0.63),
    ('Latest', ' Blog', -1.3),
    ('Latest Blog', ' Post', -1.2),
    ('DO', 'CKET', -2.35),
    ('STATES DISTRICT', ' COURT', -2.4),
    ('STATES', ' COURT', -1.6),
    ('Archive', ' Date', -1.2),
)

_BY_TOKEN = {}
for preceding, token, value in COMPLETIONS:
    _BY_TOKEN.setdefault(token, []).append((preceding, value))


def predict(token, before, position):
    for preceding, value in _BY_TOKEN.get(token, ()):
        if before.endswith(preceding):
            return value

    # Git patches and dotfiles, rather than the ordinary command name.
    if token == 'git':
        if before.endswith(' --'):
            return -4.4
        if before.endswith('.'):
            return -1.8 if before.endswith(('/.', ':.', '-- .')) else -1.1
    if token == '.com' and before.endswith('github'):
        return -1.05 if '://' in before[-20:] else -0.55
    if token == '.githubusercontent':
        return -0.7

    # Versioned MySQL dump comments, with saved OLD settings.
    if token == ' SET' and re.search(r'/\*!\d{5}$', before):
        return -4.2
    if token == 'OLD' and before.endswith('@'):
        return -2.6 if before.endswith('SET @') else -1.25

    if token in {'<tool_call>', '</tool_call>'}:
        return 0.09
    if token in {'<tool_response>', '</tool_response>'}:
        return -0.10
    if token == '<think>':
        return -0.38
    if token == ' bool':
        return 0.225
    if token == ' true':
        return 0.185
    if token == ' false':
        return 0.125

    # Source-file opening tokens differ from the same words inside a file.
    if position == 0:
        if token == '//\n':
            return -3.55
        if token in {'import', 'using', 'class', 'var', 'const', 'string'}:
            return 1.7
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != document:
        before, position = '', 0
    else:
        _, before, position = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = predict(token, before, position)
    return (document, (before + token)[-80:], position + 1), value

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 386: a mostly silent unit with a few
recognisable triggers.

Plain-language summary of what it does:
- Almost always near zero. Its large values are rare and sit on a few kinds of text.
- Strongly negative on "git" in a git diff header ("diff --git a/...", the patch text an
  agent reads back), and moderately negative on "git" in other git commands.
- Strongly negative on the variable names SET and OLD in a MySQL dump preamble
  ("/*!40101 SET @OLD_..."), and on the host pieces of a shields.io badge image URL.
- Mildly negative on domain-name pieces inside a URL (".google", ".com", ".org", ...).
- Mildly positive on the first token of each document, or of a row that starts
  mid-document, where the model has no earlier text to lean on.

The program reads only the text so far (tokens 0..t). It carries the last few
characters of the current document, the current line and the current
whitespace-free run.
"""
import re

READS = ()

GIT_DIFF = -4.4      # "git" right after "diff --"
GIT_COMMAND = -1.5   # "git" after other git text, e.g. "git diff", "git checkout"
MYSQL_SET = -3.5     # " SET" / "OLD" on a "/*!..." MySQL dump line
SHIELDS = -5.0       # host pieces ".io", "ields", "adge" of a shields.io badge URL
URL_DOMAIN = -0.12   # a dotted piece like ".com" or ".google" inside a URL
FIRST_TOKEN = 0.14   # first token of a document or row
URL_MARKERS = ("://", "www.", ".com", ".org", ".io", ".net")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix.token_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    text, line, run = ("", "", "") if carry is None or new_doc else carry
    value = 0.0
    if new_doc:
        value = FIRST_TOKEN
    if tok == "git":
        if text.endswith("diff --"):
            value = GIT_DIFF
        elif "git" in text[-12:]:
            value = GIT_COMMAND
    if line.startswith("/*!") and tok.strip() in ("SET", "OLD"):
        value = MYSQL_SET
    if "shields" in run + tok and tok in (".io", "ields", "adge"):
        value = SHIELDS
    if tok.startswith(".") and any(m in run for m in URL_MARKERS):
        value = URL_DOMAIN
    # update the carried state with this token
    line = tok.split("\n")[-1] if "\n" in tok else line + tok
    pieces = re.split(r"\s", tok)
    run = pieces[-1] if len(pieces) > 1 else run + tok
    return ((text + tok)[-40:], line[-200:], run[-200:]), value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:387 as a word-piece and word detector.

This component is almost silent. It is large only on a few specific pieces of text:

1. The syllable "era" when it is a piece of a longer word, not a word of its own:
   "Cabr|era", "d|era|iled", "Val|era", "Coom|era". Close spellings ("vera", "tera",
   "sera", "eras", "eral") and the weaker "ero"/"eros" fire too.
2. The word "serum" (with or without a leading space or a capital).
3. The Chinese characters 露 (dew; also "to expose") and 霜 (frost), and the words
   built on them, 露天 (outdoors) and 露出 (exposed).

Everywhere else the prediction is 0. Each token's value is its typical activation
(fit on training text). Whole words such as "general" or "opera" do not fire.
The activation depends only on the current token, so this program ignores context.
"""

READS = ()

# "era" as a word piece, with its typical activation.
ERA_PIECES = {
    "era": 2.5,
    "vera": 2.5,
    "tera": 2.5,
    "éra": 2.5,
    "eras": 2.5,
    "eral": 2.0,
    "sera": 1.5,
    "ero": 1.2,
    "eros": 1.2,
}

# Dew and frost characters and their compounds.
DEW_FROST = {"露": 6.5, "霜": 5.5, "露天": 4.0, "露出": 3.0}

SERUM = 4.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token in DEW_FROST:
        return carry, DEW_FROST[token]
    bare = token.strip().lower()
    if bare == "serum":
        return carry, SERUM
    if not token.startswith(" ") and bare in ERA_PIECES:
        return carry, ERA_PIECES[bare]
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection, component 389: a few token-pattern detectors.

The component is near zero almost everywhere. Its large activations come from a few
recognisable spots, each written as a rule over the current token and the text before it:

  * "df" after a non-breaking space, in runs of "df-xxx" labels: strongly positive (+3)
  * a run of middle dots "··": strongly negative (-1.6)
  * the clock suffix " am" / " pm" right after a time such as "10:24": negative (-2.5)
  * "self" as the first parameter of a method ("def f(self", Rust "&mut self"): positive (+1.2)
  * "<" right after "#include": positive (+1.3)
  * the first token of a document when it opens code or a markdown heading
    ("import", "#include", "def", "#", "##", "class", "int"): positive (+0.8)
  * "cd" as the first word of a shell command string: mildly negative (-0.6)

Everything else predicts 0, which is the component's typical value.
"""

import re

READS = ()

DOT_RUN = re.compile(r"·{2,}$")
CLOCK_END = re.compile(r"\d:\d\d$")
CODE_OPENERS = {"import", "#include", "def", "#", "##", "class", "int"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    cur = toks[-1].strip()
    prev = toks[-2] if len(toks) > 1 else ""
    before = "".join(toks[-7:-1])
    starts_doc = len(toks) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    value = 0.0
    if cur == "df" and "\xa0" in prev:
        value = 3.0
    elif DOT_RUN.match(cur):
        value = -1.6
    elif cur in ("am", "pm") and CLOCK_END.search(before):
        value = -2.5
    elif cur.lstrip("(&") == "self" and ("def " in before or "fn " in before or "&mut" in before):
        value = 1.2
    elif cur == "<" and "include" in prev:
        value = 1.3
    elif starts_doc and cur in CODE_OPENERS:
        value = 0.8
    elif cur == "cd" and prev.strip() == '"':
        value = -0.6
    return carry, float(value)

"""A string literal opening in source code (or a JSON/tool-call value), and printing calls.

The component fires on the opening quote of a string that is about to be written out as a
value: the quote after `=`, `(`, `:` (JSON), `+`, `<<`, or a print/format call. It is strongest
when the string is a format, markup, SQL or shell command. It is near zero on closing quotes,
on quotes inside prose, and on quotes in comments and includes. Printing and formatting
calls themselves (printf, echo, println, append, f-strings, `<<`) also fire, a little less.
"""
import re

READS = ()

# a quote that opens a string, with any space or bracket before it and up to two characters after
OPENER = re.compile(r'([ (=:,+\t\[{]*)(\\?)(["\'`])(.{0,2})', re.S)
# a call that writes or formats text
PRINTING = re.compile(r'\.?(?:[sS]?printf|println|print|echo|append|format|Format|log)|\(f|<<|\+=')
# how strongly an opening quote fires, by what it follows (lead) and which quote it is
STRENGTH = {
    ('(', '"'): 1.0, ('(', "'"): 0.6, ('(', '`'): 0.9,
    ('=', '"'): 0.4, ('=', "'"): 0.5,
    (' ', '"'): 0.5, (' ', "'"): 0.4, (' ', '`'): 0.1,
    ('+', '"'): 1.5, (',', '"'): 0.3, (':', '"'): 0.3, ('', '"'): 0.05,
}
SCALE = 0.6  # calibrates the sum to the component's activation


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ''
    # a value is expected after `=`, `(`, `:`, `+`, `<<` or a printing call
    value_slot = before[-1:] in ('=', '(', '+', ':') or before.endswith('<<') or PRINTING.fullmatch(before)
    context = 2.5 if value_slot else 1.0
    m = OPENER.fullmatch(token)
    if m:
        lead, escape, quote, after = m.groups()
        strength = STRENGTH.get((lead[-1:], quote), 0.0)
        if escape:
            strength = max(strength, 0.5)
        if after[:1] in ('%', '<', '\\', '/', '{'):  # format, markup or shell-escape content
            strength *= 1.8
        return None, SCALE * strength * context
    if PRINTING.fullmatch(token):
        return None, SCALE * 1.0
    return None, 0.0

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection component 392: a reference-list and link-list detector.

Mostly this component sits near zero. It goes strongly negative on the boilerplate that
opens a bibliography or link list in web and Wikipedia-style text, and mildly on other
citation and link wording. It goes mildly positive on in-text signposting ("described
below", "referred to as", "please").

The rules, in plain terms:
  * A document that opens with "Title:" gives a very large negative value on the colon.
  * A section header "References" (on its own line) is negative, and so are the next few
    tokens: the paragraph break, then "External links" (strongly on "links"), or a
    numbered list item "1".
  * Stock phrases are negative on their second word: "See also", "For more information",
    "Thank you", "Retrieved from", "Further reading".
  * Citation and link words are mildly negative: "http", "https", "literature",
    "bibliography", "sources", Chinese 来源 (source) and 参考 (reference).
  * Numbered citation markers at the start of a line ("1", then "]" or ".") are mildly negative.
  * Cross-references are mildly positive: "below" after "described", "see", "shown"; "as"
    in "referred to as"; "please" after a comma or a full stop.

Everything else predicts 0. On 1024 held-out rows this explains about 17% of the variance
(Pearson r 0.42). Putting its predictions into the model moves the next-token distribution
about 74% as far as switching the component off does (KL 1.8e-5 vs 2.5e-5 nats per
position). The rest is small diffuse
activity (std about 0.07) with no clean token or topic pattern.

Main program: `step` looks at the newest token (and the one before it, within the same
document) and carries a count of how many tokens have passed since a "References" header.
"""

READS = ()

# Words that mark bibliography, link or source material (negative on the word itself).
CITATION_WORDS = {
    "links": -1.6, "https": -0.6, "http": -0.3, "literature": -0.3, "bibliography": -0.3,
    "isbn": -0.3, "retrieved": -0.2, "reading": -0.15, "reference": -0.15, "sources": -0.1,
    "来源": -2.9, "参考": -1.1, "資料": -0.5, "情報": -0.3,
}

# (previous word, word) stock phrases: the value goes on the second word.
STOCK_PHRASES = {
    ("see", "also"): -1.4,
    ("more", "information"): -0.7,
    ("thank", "you"): -0.6,
    ("retrieved", "from"): -0.5,
    ("obtained", "from"): -0.5,
    ("taken", "from"): -0.5,
    ("further", "reading"): -3.0,
    ("to", "as"): 0.8,       # "referred to as"
    (",", "please"): 0.5,
    (".", "please"): 0.4,
}

# Words after which a following "below" points forward to later text.
DESCRIBING = {"described", "discussed", "see", "shown", "explained", "detail", "listed",
              "seen", "illustrated", "mentioned"}

# Tokens after a "References" header: (age, word) -> value. Age 1 is the token right after it.
HEADER_FOLLOW = {"links": -4.3}


def _header_value(age, word):
    """Value for the tokens that follow a 'References' header, `age` tokens after it."""
    if word in HEADER_FOLLOW:
        return HEADER_FOLLOW[word]
    if age == 1:
        return -2.6          # the paragraph break after the header
    if age == 2 and word == "1":
        return -3.0          # first item of a numbered reference list
    if age == 2:
        return -0.5
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = raw.strip().lower()
    new_doc = len(prefix) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_doc:
        prev_raw, prev_word, prev2_raw, age = "", "", "", None
    else:
        prev_raw = prefix.token_strings[-2]
        prev_word = prev_raw.strip().lower()
        prev2_raw = prefix.token_strings[-3] if len(prefix) > 2 else ""
        age = None if carry is None else carry + 1
    # Is the previous token the first token of its document? (then "Title" opens the document)
    prev_opens_doc = len(prefix) == 2 or (
        len(prefix) > 2 and prefix.document_ids[-3] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    )

    value = CITATION_WORDS.get(word, 0.0)
    value = STOCK_PHRASES.get((prev_word, word), value)
    if word == "below" and prev_word in DESCRIBING:
        value = 1.5
    if word == "1" and "\n" in prev_raw:
        value = -0.5
    if word in ("]", ".", "]:") and prev_word == "1" and ("\n" in prev2_raw or prev2_raw.strip() == "["):
        value = -0.5
    if prev_word == "title" and word == ":" and prev_opens_doc:
        value = -12.3

    if raw.strip() == "References" and "\n" in prev_raw:
        age, value = 0, -2.0
    elif age is not None and age <= 3:
        value = _header_value(age, word) or value
    if age is not None and age > 3:
        age = None
    return age, value

"""A lexical approximation of a mostly negative software-terminology response.

Recognize semantic families of programming words, with regular inflections
and partial-word completion. Family strength depends on leading whitespace
and a fading software-topic signal. Keep a shorter after-effect of technical
words. Small corrections cover row starts, paths, diagnostics, and formatting.
This does not try to explain miscellaneous positive token-specific responses.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache

READS = ()

# Family name, vocabulary, then (base, whitespace bonus, topic bonus).
FAMILIES = (

"""Layer-1 MLP neuron 393 (down_proj), read as a 'software-jargon' detector.

What it does, in plain terms:
  * It dips negative on words from the working vocabulary of software: command-line tools
    and their arguments ("command", "arguments", "bash", "install"), errors and warnings,
    and everyday dev nouns and verbs ("file", "code", "directory", "config", "test", "run").
    The deepest dips are on command, argument, install and error words.
  * How deep a dip is depends on the jargon already seen in the same document: in
    technical stretches (agent transcripts, build logs, terminal output) the same word
    dips further, and ordinary tokens dip a little too.
  * The first token of each document gets a small positive push.
  * Everything else is about zero.

The program keeps a running jargon density for the current document: an exponential
average of how often jargon words appeared, reset at each document start.
"""

READS = ()

# Strong: commands, arguments, installs, compilers, errors and warnings.
STRONG = set("""
command commands cmd bash args arg argument arguments install installed installation
compile compiler compiled directory error errors warning warnings exit invalid interpreter
executable usr usage
""".split())

# Mild: the rest of software work: files and paths, code and configs, packages and tools,
# tests and builds, logs and output, errors and failures, programming nouns.
MILD = set("""
file files filename folder folders path paths dir dirs config configure configuration
default version versions npm git package packages run running execute execution test tests
failed failing fail failure failures output console build builds debug log logs logging logger
setup parameter parameters params param module modules plugin plugins api repo repository
pass passed hooks hook code library libs dependency dependencies env environment variable
variables script scripts shell terminal sudo option options flag flags stdout stderr print
timeout issue issues bug bugs fix fixed server client http url token auth ssl hash commit
branch clone download downloaded upload docker container image cache temp root home bin lib
exception traceback deprecated unexpected undefined null empty string strings array returns
changes method methods class function properly successfully expected snippet tool tools
github php python node pip yarn make
""".split())

DECAY = 0.98       # how slowly the jargon density fades
DOC_START = 0.32   # small push on the first token of each document


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """carry = the jargon density so far in this document (None at a row start)."""
    new_doc = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    density = 0.0 if (carry is None or new_doc) else carry

    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    strong = word in STRONG
    mild = word in MILD and not strong

    if new_doc:
        value = DOC_START
    else:
        value = -0.67 * strong - 0.20 * mild
        value -= density * (0.86 + 2.3 * strong + 1.66 * mild)

    jargon = 1.0 if (strong or mild) else 0.0
    new_density = DECAY * density + (1 - DECAY) * jargon
    return new_density, value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:394: a "first token of a document" response.

What it does: the component is silent inside a document, but at the first token of each
document it writes a large negative value. A document starts at the beginning of a packed
row and after every document boundary, where the model has no earlier text to look at.
The size depends only on that token: about -12.5 if the token contains a letter (words,
names, CJK characters), and about -8 for digits, punctuation, symbols and whitespace.
If the document so far is one token repeated over and over (for example a long run of
'⎯' or '····'), the same value carries on for the whole run. Everywhere else it is 0.

Why: at a document's first token, attention can only see the token itself, so the
residual stream there depends on the token alone. This is that first-token state.
"""

import unicodedata

READS = ()

WORD_VALUE = -12.5   # first token contains a letter
OTHER_VALUE = -8.0   # digits, punctuation, symbols, whitespace


def first_token_value(text):
    """The response to a document's first token, from its text."""
    if any(unicodedata.category(c).startswith("L") for c in text):
        return WORD_VALUE
    return OTHER_VALUE


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_ids[-1]
    new_document = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_document:
        value = first_token_value(prefix.token_strings[-1])
        return (token, value), value
    if carry is not None and carry[0] == token:

        return carry, carry[1]
    return None, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:395 -- a sparse 'or' detector.

The component is quiet almost everywhere (it fires on about 0.1% of tokens) and
its big values are all tied to the word "or" and to the letters "or" written
after an "s":

1. After the conjunction "or":
   - "two" or "so" in an approximate-quantity idiom ("an hour or two",
     "a week or so", "one or two") pushes the activation strongly negative (about -8);
   - "both" after "or" is also negative (about -4.5);
   - "else" ("... or else") is strongly positive (about +8.5);
   - "otherwise" ("... or otherwise", common in legal text) is mildly positive (about +3.3).
2. Word-internal "or" that follows a piece ending in "s" (as in "vis|oria",
   "vers|org", "sens|ory", "Vorsorge") is negative (about -3).
3. Whole words "sor", "sour", "sore", "sensory" and Cyrillic "сор" are negative (about -5).

Everything else predicts 0. The values are the typical activations in those
contexts, not fitted per-token. What the simple version gets: the sharp idiom
spikes and the "s-or" spelling, which carry most of the variance. What it leaves out:
the many weak, mixed-sign "or"-fragments inside foreign words (e.g. "ignor", "ang|or"),
which a per-token table would capture only partly.

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    cur = raw.strip().lower()
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if len(prefix) > 1 else ""
    if prev == "or":
        if cur in ("two", "so"):
            return None, -8.0
        if cur == "both":
            return None, -4.5
        if cur == "else":
            return None, 8.5
        if cur == "otherwise":
            return None, 3.3
    if raw[:1].isalpha() and raw.lower().startswith("or") and prev.endswith("s"):
        return None, -3.0
    if cur in ("sor", "sour", "sensory", "sore") or cur.startswith("сор"):
        return None, -5.0
    return None, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:396 -- a sparse, mostly-silent component.

What it does, in plain terms:
  * Leader-dot filler: a run of the middle-dot token '··' (as in tables of
    contents) drives it to a steady negative value, about -1.
  * First token of a document: the component sits slightly negative (about -0.2),
    since with nothing before it the token is read on its own.
  * Everywhere else it is predicted as 0. Its large positive spikes sit on the
    letter k (or Greek kappa, Cyrillic ka, Arabic kaf) when it is a piece of a
    longer word split across tokens, typically a name or loanword, e.g.
    "Shish|k|ina", "Mah|jong|g", "Jang|ka". Those spikes are not predictable from
    the token or its neighbour, so this program leaves them at 0.
"""

READS = ()

DOT_RUN = "··"
DOC_START = -0.2
DOT_VALUE = -0.97


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    t = prefix.position
    if t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]:
        return carry, DOC_START
    if tokens[-1] == DOT_RUN:
        return carry, DOT_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

"""A spelling-fragment predictor, with an explicit language heuristic.

It responds mainly to short subwords containing soft-c spellings, z or ç,
including the next piece of the same word. Common fused suffixes are weaker
cues. Decaying function-word counts modulate the response by language.
Isolated Cyrillic ц, following word pieces, and Japanese ji kana get small
positive estimates. This captures a tendency, not the rare large peaks.
"""
import re

READS = ()
ROMANCE = set('''
    el los las del una unos unas por para que con pero como su sus esto esta
    de y ao aos uma um dos das pelo pela não nas nos os em na do da des les
    une dans pour avec et est du au aux il lo gli della delle che per di le un
'''.split())
ENGLISH = set('''
    the of and to in is it that for with was on are as be this have not from
    or by at an they you which their had has but we his her them its
'''.split())
SLAVIC = set('''
    się jest nie na do że to jak dla przez oraz ale czy są po za od ze tym
    tego se je a v ve s z pro jsou když tak na ale jako
'''.split())
TURKISH = set('''
    bir ve bu için ile de da çok daha ne var olan olarak her en gibi ama
    ben o mi
'''.split())
LANGUAGES = (ROMANCE, ENGLISH, SLAVIC, TURKISH)
WORDS = re.compile(r'[^\W\d_]+')
SOFT_C = re.compile(r'c[eiéèêëíìîïy]')
# Productive nominal/adjectival endings and English -ize forms.
FUSED_ENDING = re.compile(
    r'^(?:iz(?:e[dsr]?s?|ing|ations?|ab(?:le|ility))|'
    r'[aiu]?[cç](?:i[oó]ne?s?|[aã]o|ões)|[ai]zioni?|'
    r'[ae]n(?:ce|cy|cia)s?|[ai]?c(?:ial(?:ly)?|ious(?:ly)?|ians?|ity|ism))$'
)


def confidence(scores, language):
    others = max(v for i, v in enumerate(scores) if i != language)
    margin = (scores[language] - others) / max(1., sum(scores) * .35)
    return max(0., min(1., margin))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', (0.,) * 4, False)
    _, prior, scores, previous_ts = carry
    s = text.lower()
    words = WORDS.findall(s)
    scores = tuple(
        old * .96 + sum(w in dictionary for w in words)
        for old, dictionary in zip(scores, LANGUAGES)
    )

        .8 * any(ch in s for ch in 'ñãõ'), 0.,
        .8 * any(ch in s for ch in 'łżźąęřůěčšžďť'),
        .8 * any(ch in s for ch in 'ığş')
    )
    scores = tuple(a + b for a, b in zip(scores, letter_evidence))
    romance, slavic, turkish = (
        confidence(scores, i) for i in (0, 2, 3)
    )

    continued = bool(s and s[0].isalpha() and prior)
    prior = prior if continued else ''
    fused = bool(FUSED_ENDING.fullmatch(s))
    c = SOFT_C.search(s)
    cross_c = bool(prior.endswith('c') and s[:1] in 'eiéèêëíìîïy')
    short_c = bool(c and c.start() <= 1 and not fused and (
        len(s) <= 4 and not re.search(r'c[ei][bcdfghjklmnpqrstvwxz]{2}', s)
        or re.search(r'c[ie][aeiou]', s)
        or s.endswith(('ar', 'er', 'ir', 'ado', 'ido', 'endo', 'ento', 'iento'))
    ))
    z = s.find('z')
    short_z = z >= 0 and z <= 1 and not fused and len(s) <= 6
    back_vowel_z = bool(re.search(r'[ao]z|z[ao]', s))
    old_c = list(SOFT_C.finditer(prior))
    recent_c = bool(old_c and len(prior) - old_c[-1].end() <= 2)
    recent_z = 'z' in prior and len(prior) - prior.rfind('z') <= 3
    recent_cedilla = 'ç' in prior and len(prior) - prior.rfind('ç') <= 3

    value += .232 * (text.strip() in ('ジ', 'じ'))

"""Layer-1 MLP component 397: a weak negative response to word pieces of Romance words.

What it does
- Looks at the current token only if it continues a word: letters only, no leading
  space, right after another letter piece of the same word (e.g. "Pro|z|esse",
  "fun|z|ionario", "del|ici|osa", "almor|z|ar").
- Scores how strongly the piece is spelled with Romance-style consonants:
  1.0 for z or ç, 0.6 for a soft c (ci, ce), 0.2 for other c, 0.1 otherwise.
- Scores how Romance the recent text is: the share of Spanish/Portuguese/Italian/French
  function words among the last 25 tokens of the same document, against English ones.
- Predicts  -weight * (0.1 + romance_share)  on such pieces and 0 everywhere else.

Why: the component's large values are almost all negative, and they fall on exactly
these pieces inside Romance words. Its sign flips to positive in Slavic and Turkish
spellings and it is near 0 in English. The predictor captures only a small share of the
variance; the size of the response varies with context in ways a short rule does not
model, and a per-token table would do better on training rows but is not a concept.
"""

import re

READS = ()

ROMANCE_WORDS = set(
    "de la el que los las y en con para una un es por del se su al lo como pero le o "
    "não uma os do da um ao mais ele foi são di che il per sono della anche le nel "
    "des du est une les qui dans pour pas sur avec et au aux ce sont nous ils elle".split()
)
ENGLISH_WORDS = set(
    "the and of to in is that it for with as on was be by this are at or from have an "
    "not but which you he his they we her she their there been has were will would can".split()
)
WINDOW = 25  # recent tokens used to judge the language


def weight(low):
    """How strongly a piece's spelling marks a Romance word."""
    if "z" in low or "ç" in low:
        return 1.0
    if re.search(r"c[ei]", low):
        return 0.6
    if "c" in low:
        return 0.2
    return 0.1

    t = prefix.position
    piece = prefix.token_strings[t]
    same_doc = t > 0 and prefix.document_ids[t - 1] == prefix.document_ids[t]
    # the piece must continue a word: letters, no leading space, after a letter piece
    if not same_doc or piece[:1] == " " or not piece.isalpha():
        return carry, 0.0
    previous = prefix.token_strings[t - 1]
    if previous[:1] == " " or not previous.isalpha():
        return carry, 0.0
    # the language cue: function words in the recent text of this document
    start = t - WINDOW + 1
    while start < 0 or prefix.document_ids[start] != prefix.document_ids[t]:
        start += 1
    text = "".join(prefix.token_strings[start : t + 1]).lower()
    words = re.findall(r"[^\W\d_]+", text)

    english = sum(w in ENGLISH_WORDS for w in words)
    share = romance / (romance + english + 1)
    return carry, -weight(piece.lower()) * (0.1 + share)

"""Document-onset spikes and a small textual-boilerplate response.

clauses get negative corrections. These are approximations, not word lookups.

import re
import unicodedata
from functools import lru_cache

               'she her hers it its they them their theirs'.split())

LINKERS = set('of to in for on at by with from as into over under about '
              'through between among against without within during before '
              'after until since upon per via be am is are was were been '
              'being have has had do does did can could may might shall '
              'should will would must'.split())

          list(calendar.month_abbr)[1:]} | {'sept'}

            'infringement liability liable permission distribute '
            'redistribution reproduction reserve limitation condition notice'.split())
MEDIA = set('article paper blog post page reply message review publication '
            'website document newsletter text video chapter book'.split())


@lru_cache(maxsize=16000)
def word_kinds(s):
    w = s.strip().lower()
    forms = set(wordnet.base_forms(w)) | {w} if w.isalpha() else {w}
    return w, bool(forms & LEGAL), bool(forms & MEDIA)

        return 1.10 if s == '\t' else 1.01
    if s == '\x00': return -0.82
    if s.startswith('<|'): return -0.03
    if s.startswith(('/*', '//', '#!', '---')): return -0.12
    if s.lstrip().startswith('#'): return -0.08
    if s.isspace() or s in ('\\n', '\\r\\n'):
        return 0.45 if '\n' in s or '\\n' in s else 0.23
    if w in ARTICLES: return -0.04
    if w in PRONOUNS: return 0.38
    if w in LINKERS: return 0.27
    if len(s.strip()) == 1 and s.strip().isupper(): return -0.065
    if s.strip().isnumeric(): return 0.095

    if s == '</think>': value += 0.16

    if s == '.md': value -= 0.146

    'divisible division raise square ratio proportional equal compare scale '

    if t in SIGNS:
        value += SIGNS[t][int(token[:1].isspace())]

    elif '/' in t and re.fullmatch(r'[)\]]*/[(\[]*',t): value += .75
    elif t in ('×','÷','±','≤','≥','≠'): value += .33
    elif t in ('==','!=','===','!=='): value -= .01

        if re.search(r'(^|\n)[ \t]+\S[^\n]*$',history): value += .08

    value += RELATIONS.get(w,0)

    if age<=8: value += RECENT.get(operation,{}).get(w,0)

    operation, age = (sorted(recent)[0],1) if recent else (operation,age+1)

What it is: a detector for the words and symbols of arithmetic and of comparison. It
responds to the verb or symbol that names an operation or relation between two quantities:
subtract / minus / multiply / divide / squared / exceeds (strongest), then times / twice /
half / double / equal / greater / less / mod and the operators ), /, ×, ÷, +=, -=, >=, <=, :=

"the", "of" or "between" right after an operation word ("subtract the", "square of").
Measurement nouns and unit or code identifiers (count, length, size, radius, threshold,
kg, px, .length) are slightly negative. Everything else is 0.

predictions are on the component's own scale.

short pieces, glued on with no space.

that is glued directly onto a short piece before it:

case pieces, and silent on common word endings (s, ing, ed, ...), on whole words, and on

context, so the rule explains only a few percent of the variance.

    "s es ed ing er ers ly y al ion tion ment ness ism ist ic ical ity ies en ure ant ent "
    "able ous ive ful less est".split()

ENDING = 0.01

SHORT_PAIR = 0.06  # other short pieces: first at most 2 letters, second at most 3

What it responds to (all other positions predict 0):

1. The first token of a document (or of a packed row): a steady dip, about -0.37. The
   model has no context there, and this component is pushed negative.

    "Eq.", "Eqs.", "Fig.", "Figs.", "Figure", "Table", "Section", "Theorem", "Lemma",
    "Proposition", "Corollary", "Conjecture", "Property", "Definition", "Remark", "Equation",
)

    " shown", " defined", " discussed", " described", " given", " as", " depicted",
    " presented", " obtained", " outlined", " mentioned", " revealed", " indicated",

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]

    first = len(prefix.token_strings) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]

    flags = [] if first else carry

    if "·" in token:

after verbs not on these lists, gives nothing. The lists are what matter: a generic
"verb + preposition" rule does not work, because "verb + to" in general averages to zero.
The program does not model the component's negative side (rare Chinese characters,
repeated junk tokens) or its small background noise.

The program reads only the newest token and the one before it, within the same
document. Predictions are a fixed value per word list.
"""

READS = ()

PREPOSITIONS = {"for", "to", "through", "over", "upon", "on", "from", "across", "out", "down", "along", "against"}

# Verbs of calling, appealing, passing and arguing (strong), e.g. "call for", "appeal to", "pass through".
STRONG = {
    "call", "calls", "called", "calling", "appeal", "appeals", "appealed", "appealing",
    "pass", "passes", "passed", "passing", "argue", "argues", "argued", "arguing",
    "attend", "attends", "attended", "attending",
}
# Verbs and nouns of failing, appearing, caring, advocating, hearing (medium), e.g. "fail to", "care for".
MEDIUM = {
    "fail", "fails", "failed", "failing", "failure", "appear", "appears", "appeared",
    "care", "cares", "cared", "caring", "advocate", "advocates", "advocated", "pray", "praying",
    "cater", "proceed", "proceeded", "hear", "heard", "hearing", "hesitate", "cease", "ceased",
    "witness", "argument", "arguments", "petition", "as",
}
# Verbs of looking, hoping, viewing, going (weak), e.g. "look for", "hope for".
WEAK = {
    "look", "looks", "looked", "looking", "hope", "hopes", "hoped", "hoping", "view", "viewed",
    "seen", "evidence", "case", "forward", "take", "go", "goes", "went", "gone", "going", "watch",
}

STRONG_VALUE, MEDIUM_VALUE, WEAK_VALUE = 2.7, 1.1, 0.3


def _word(text):
    return text.strip().lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    ids = prefix.token_ids
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    if len(ids) < 2 or docs[-2] != docs[-1]:
        return carry, 0.0
    if _word(prefix.token_strings[-1]) not in PREPOSITIONS:
        return carry, 0.0
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    word = _word(before)
    if word in STRONG or (before == "As" and word == "as"):
        return carry, STRONG_VALUE
    if word in MEDIUM:
        return carry, MEDIUM_VALUE
    if word in WEAK:
        return carry, WEAK_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

programs.sol:
"""Approximate a response to short grave-accented Latin fragments.

Bare lowercase grave vowels get large predictions. Recent function words
and Vietnamese spelling clues select a language-dependent scale (French
is the fallback). Onset, coda and extra vowel marks modulate Vietnamese
fragments; a following vowel can complete a falling-tone diphthong.
Slashed-o fragments get a smaller positive response, repeated middle dots
a negative one. Other text stays near zero. Context resets per document.
"""
import re
import unicodedata as ud

READS = ()
FRENCH_FUNCTION_WORDS = frozenset(
    'le les des une et pour dans est du au sur pas avec sont ce ces '
    'en qui aux'.split()
)
ITALIAN_FUNCTION_WORDS = frozenset(
    'il gli lo della che di del per non una sono con e si degli alla nel '
    'nella delle anche'.split()
)
VIETNAMESE_FUNCTION_WORDS = frozenset(
    'và của là có không những được cho trong một người này đã để các với'.split()
)


def language(context):
    words = re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]+', context.lower())
    french = sum(w in FRENCH_FUNCTION_WORDS for w in words)
    italian = sum(w in ITALIAN_FUNCTION_WORDS for w in words)
    vietnamese = sum(w in VIETNAMESE_FUNCTION_WORDS for w in words)
    decomposed = ud.normalize('NFD', context.lower())
    # Breve, horn, hook above and dot below are Vietnamese spelling clues.
    if ('đ' in context.lower() or any(
            c in decomposed for c in '\u0306\u031b\u0309\u0323')):
        vietnamese += 4
    if vietnamese >= 2:
        return 'vi'
    return 'it' if italian > french else 'fr'


def response(token, context):
    word = token.strip()
    if word == 'ø':
        return 0.85 if token == word else 0.45
    if word and set(word) == {'·'} and len(word) > 1:
        return -0.68
    accents = [i for i, c in enumerate(word)
               if '\u0300' in ud.normalize('NFD', c)]
    if not accents:
        # An unaccented letter can finish a Vietnamese falling-tone diphthong.
        if len(token) == 1 and token in 'iouy' and context:
            last = ud.normalize('NFD', context[-1])
            if (len(last) == 2 and last[0] in 'aeiou'
                    and last[1] == '\u0300' and language(context) == 'vi'):
                return 3.8
        return -0.003
    i = accents[0]
    vowel = ud.normalize('NFD', word[i])
    if vowel[0] not in 'aeiou' or len(word) > 6:
        return 0.0
    onset, coda = word[:i].lower(), word[i+1:].lower()
    lang = language(context)
    if lang == 'vi':
        value = 8.0 if vowel[0] == 'u' else 6.0
        if onset or token != word:
            value = 2.4
        if coda:
            value *= 0.65 if len(coda) == 1 else 0.3
        # An additional horn, breve or circumflex weakens the grave response.
        if len(vowel) > 2:
            value *= 0.4
        if onset.startswith(('l', 'n', 'v', 'g')):
            value *= 0.15
        return value
    if token == word and len(word) == 1:
        if context.endswith(('-', "'", '’')):
            return -0.3
        if vowel[0] == 'e':
            return 1.1 if lang == 'it' else 4.8
        return 0.4 if lang == 'it' else 1.2
    if len(word) == 1:
        return 0.1
    if vowel[0] == 'e' and not coda and len(onset) <= 2:
        return 1.4
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    context = '' if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = response(token, context)
    return (doc, (context + token)[-256:]), float(value)

"""Grave-accented letters and words, and the first token of a document.

Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:415 is quiet almost everywhere. It switches on for a
grave-accented vowel (è most of all, then ù, à, ì, ò) written as a bare piece of a word,
with no space before it: the è in French words like "espèce", "lèvres", "événements",
"indigènes", "Règlement". It also fires on a few Vietnamese words with the grave tone
(" bà", " thì", " màu", " rồi"). On the first token of a document, with no earlier text
to look back on, it sits slightly negative.

The program predicts those values and 0 elsewhere.
"""

READS = ()

# Activation to predict on a grave-accented token, read off the training rows.
GRAVE_TOKEN = {
    "è": 3.9,
    "ù": 2.9,
    "à": 0.6,
    "ì": 0.7,
    "ò": 0.7,
    " bà": 3.2,
    " thì": 2.5,
    " rồi": 2.5,
    " màu": 1.25,
}

# Activation on the first token of a document (no preceding context).
DOCUMENT_START = -0.22


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Predict this position's activation from its token and whether it opens a document."""
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if len(prefix.token_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return carry, DOCUMENT_START
    return carry, GRAVE_TOKEN.get(token, 0.0)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:416 - a "year digit" detector.

The component fires on the last digit of a year written as 20X, i.e. the
'1' or '2' in 2010-2029 (as in "... 20|1|9", "... 20|2|0"). It is near zero
on every other digit, and on the 0 that starts such a year.

It also fires weakly on the "ox" family of words (oxygen, oxide, oxidation,
oxy-, toxic, Oxford, Cox, ...), but not on "box", "prox", "approx".

Prediction: 8.0 for '1' and 10.5 for '2' after "20"; 5.0 on "ox"-words;
0 elsewhere. The year rule carries most of the variance.
"""

READS = ()

OX_EXCLUDE = ("box", "prox", "approx")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings
    t = len(s) - 1
    cur = s[t].lower()
    # Year digit: the 1 or 2 right after the two tokens "2", "0".
    if cur in ("1", "2") and t >= 2 and s[t - 1] == "0" and s[t - 2] == "2":
        return carry, (8.0 if cur == "1" else 10.5)
    # Oxygen family: the token contains "ox" but is not box/prox/approx.
    if "ox" in cur and not any(w in cur for w in OX_EXCLUDE):
        return carry, 5.0
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 417: an "asterisk and 此" detector.

What it does: this component writes a negative value whenever the current token is
an asterisk used as a symbol, and a more negative value on the Chinese word 此 ("this",
as in 在此, 从此, 至此, 如此). It is near zero everywhere else.

  * Asterisk symbols: the tokens " *" and "*" (multiplication, bullets, footnote marks,
    comment-block stars), and the operator-like forms "(*", ".*", ")*", "※" and "＊".
    Bold and comment markers ("**", "/*", "*/") and star-plus-letter tokens ("*e",
    "*x") are excluded: they are near zero or positive. Average activation is about -1.3.
  * Formal Chinese demonstratives 此 and 彼 (and compounds such as 在此, 至此, 此时,
    如此, 彼此). Average about -3, and -6 on bare 此. 因此 ("therefore") is left out: it is
    common and only weakly negative.

Why this and not a table: the simple rules above explain about a quarter of the
variance on the training sample. A full per-token lookup table explains about 44%,
but its extra entries are many small, unrelated token effects, so they are not
readable as a concept.
"""

READS = ()


def is_asterisk_symbol(token):
    """True for an asterisk or ※ used as a symbol (operator, bullet, footnote mark)."""
    if token in ("*", "＊", "※"):
        return True
    if "*" not in token or "**" in token or "/" in token or "\\" in token:
        return False
    return not any(c.isalnum() for c in token)


def is_formal_this(token):
    """True for 此 / 彼 and their compounds, except 因此 ("therefore")."""
    return ("此" in token or "彼" in token) and token != "因此"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if is_formal_this(token):
        return None, -3.0
    if is_asterisk_symbol(token):
        return None, -1.3
    return None, 0.0

programs.sol:
"""A detector for Romance clitic-pronoun forms at word beginnings.

Recent completed words supply a dictionary-frequency estimate of language.
This distinguishes English 'me', Spanish 'si', or Dutch 'te' from clitics.
Preceding pronouns, negation, and relative words boost clitic readings; forms
also used as articles get a smaller baseline. Standalone French apostrophes
and two split preverbal particles have separate rules. Everything else
receives zero. Amplitudes were fitted on training data; this is a lexical
and grammatical approximation, not a full parse. No future text is used.
"""
import math
import re
from functools import lru_cache
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
LANGUAGES = ('en', 'fr', 'es', 'it', 'pt', 'ro', 'de', 'cs', 'nl', 'tr', 'hu')

# Approximate activation levels for recognizable function-word forms.
# The French 'se' entry adds to its shared Romance value.
SHARED = {'me': 9.755, 'te': 9.543, 'se': 6.434}
FRENCH = {'s': 3.407,
    'm': 1.879,
    't': 0.755,
    'vous': 5.126,
    'nous': 5.466,
    'ne': 2.309,
    'le': 1.709,
    'la': 0.562,
    'les': 1.291,
    'lui': 5.062,
    'leur': 4.851,
    'en': 0.842,
    'y': 2.423,
    'se': 3.223}
ITALIAN = {'mi': 8.993,
    'ti': 7.653,
    'ci': 10.611,
    'vi': 6.833,
    'si': 7.437,
    'gli': 4.365,
    'li': 7.783,
    'se': 1.022,
    'ne': 5.23,
    'lo': 5.107,
    'le': 1.709,
    'la': 0.562}
SPANISH = {'nos': 13.016,
    'lo': 2.784,
    'le': 7.914,
    'la': 0.562,
    'les': 5.725,
    'los': 1.011,
    'las': 1.011}
PORTUGUESE = {'nos': 4.454, 'o': 1.214, 'os': 1.214, 'as': 1.214}
FRENCH_OBJECT_BOOST = {'s': 5.669,
    'm': 6.684,
    't': 3.81,
    'vous': 7.956,
    'nous': 7.956,
    'y': 4.203,
    'en': 3.244,
    'lui': 3.454,
    'leur': 3.155}
ELISION = {'s': 10.289,
    'm': 7.323,
    't': 4.002,
    'j': 3.331,
    'n': 3.037,
    'l': 1.291,
    'd': 0.731,
    'c': 2.234}
HISTORY = 12
SHARPNESS = 4
ARTICLE_BOOST = 3.13
CLITIC_BOOST = 4.479
ADVERB_ELISION = 5.031
PERSIAN_PREFIX = 9.169
GREEK_PARTICLE = 1.353

FRENCH_PREVERBAL_CUES = set('je tu il elle on nous vous ils elles ne qui'.split())
ITALIAN_PREVERBAL_CUES = set('io tu lui lei noi voi loro non si'.split())
SPANISH_PREVERBAL_CUES = set('yo tú él ella nosotros vosotros ellos ellas no se que'.split())
ARTICLES = {'le', 'la', 'les', 'los', 'las'}
FORMS = set(SHARED) | set(FRENCH) | set(ITALIAN) | set(SPANISH) | set(PORTUGUESE)

@lru_cache(maxsize=80000)
def word_scores(word):
    return tuple(zipf_frequency(word, language) for language in LANGUAGES)


def language_weights(history):
    if not history:
        return (.63, .10, .08, .06, .05, .02, .02, .01, .01, .01, .01)
    scores = [sum(column) / len(history) for column in zip(*history)]
    peak = max(scores)
    weights = [math.exp(SHARPNESS * (score - peak)) for score in scores]
    total = sum(weights)
    return tuple(weight / total for weight in weights)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', [], '', '')
    _, pending, history, previous, last_token = carry
    old_pending = pending
    if text.startswith('<|') or text in {
        '<think>', '</think>', 'assistant', 'user', 'system'
    }:
        return (doc, pending, history, previous, text), 0.0
    # Accumulate Latin-1 word spans across tokenizer fragments.
    for piece in re.findall(r'[A-Za-zÀ-ÖØ-öø-ÿ]+|[^A-Za-zÀ-ÖØ-öø-ÿ]+', text):
        if piece[0].isalpha() and ord(piece[0]) < 256:
            pending += piece.lower()
        elif pending:
            previous = pending
            history = (history + [word_scores(pending)])[-HISTORY:]
            pending = ''
    carry = (doc, pending, history, previous, text)
    form = text.strip().lower()
    boundary = text[:1].isspace() or (
        not old_pending and (not last_token or not last_token[-1].isalnum())
    )
    apostrophe = text[:1] in {"'", '’'} and len(text) < 5
    persian = text == 'ی' and last_token == ' م'  # Split Persian می.
    greek = text == 'α' and last_token.endswith('ν')  # Split Greek να.
    if not ((boundary and form in FORMS) or apostrophe or persian or greek):
        return carry, 0.0
    _, fr, es, it, pt, ro, *_ = language_weights(history)
    value = 0.0
    if boundary:
        value = SHARED.get(form, 0.0) * (fr + es + pt + ro)
        value += fr * FRENCH.get(form, 0.0) + it * ITALIAN.get(form, 0.0)
        value += es * SPANISH.get(form, 0.0) + pt * PORTUGUESE.get(form, 0.0)
        french_object = previous in FRENCH_PREVERBAL_CUES
        if french_object:
            value += fr * FRENCH_OBJECT_BOOST.get(form, 0.0)
        if form in ARTICLES:
            value += ARTICLE_BOOST * (
                fr * french_object
                + it * (previous in ITALIAN_PREVERBAL_CUES)
                + es * (previous in SPANISH_PREVERBAL_CUES)
            )
        if form in {'me', 'te', 'nos'}:
            value += CLITIC_BOOST * (
                fr * french_object + es * (previous in SPANISH_PREVERBAL_CUES)
            )
        if form in {'mi', 'ti', 'ci', 'vi'}:
            value += CLITIC_BOOST * it * (previous in ITALIAN_PREVERBAL_CUES)
        if form == 'me' and previous == 'let':
            value = 0.0  # English 'let me', not a Romance clitic.
    if apostrophe:
        if text in {"'", '’'}:
            value += (fr + it) * ELISION.get(old_pending, 0.0)
        if form[1:] in {'en', 'y'}:
            value += fr * ADVERB_ELISION
    if persian:
        value += PERSIAN_PREFIX
    if greek:
        value += GREEK_PARTICLE
    # Case-only variants are weaker, especially all-capital abbreviations.
    if len(form) > 1 and text.strip().isupper():
        value *= 0.15
    elif text.strip()[:1].isupper():
        value *= 0.85
    return carry, float(value)

"""Romance object/reflexive clitic pronouns that sit right before a verb.

In French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese and similar text, a short object or reflexive
pronoun (se, me, te, nos, vous, le, si, s', n' ...) placed before a conjugated verb
("elle se jeta", "que me ama", "il s'occupe") drives this component high. The same word
used as an article, conjunction or inside an English word stays near 0, so the program
only fires when the 16 preceding words look Romance (more Romance function words than
English ones). Pronouns get a boost after a subject or relative word (que, qui, il, nous).
Split verb particles written as two tokens (Persian mi- as م+ی, Bulgarian се as с+е,
Greek να as ν+α) also fire. Output is scaled by 0.8 (fit to the activations).
"""
READS = ()
ROMANCE_WORDS = set("de la le les des du et que qui il elle ils elles nous vous je tu se en y es est son con por para los las una di che non per sono della dans une pour avec sur ne lo el".split())
ENGLISH_WORDS = set("the and of to is that it for with you was he she they this are be on as at by from or not have has my which what will can".split())
CLITIC = {"nos": 11, "nous": 7, "vous": 7, "te": 7, "me": 7, "ci": 7, "lui": 6, "leur": 5, "ti": 5, "se": 5, "gli": 5,
          "si": 3, "li": 3, "lo": 2.5, "le": 2.2, "les": 1.5, "vi": 3, "m": 1.7, "ne": 1.5, "s": 2.7, "los": 1.2,
          "las": 0.9, "la": 0.6, "l": 0.9, "os": 1.0, "en": 0.5, "y": 0.2}
PREP_DET = set("de du des dans sur sous par pour avec sans entre vers chez contre à a en un une el la los las le les al del".split())
PRE_VERB = set("qui que il elle ils elles je tu nous vous on se ne n y et ou no ya".split())
ELIDE = set("s n m t qu".split())
def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = tok.strip().lower()
    standalone = tok.startswith(" ") or tok[:1].isupper()
    words = [s.strip().lower() for s in prefix.token_strings[-16:]]
    prev = words[-2] if len(words) > 1 else ""
    value = 0.0
    if standalone and word in CLITIC:
        value = CLITIC[word]
        if word in ("le", "la", "les", "l", "los", "las") and prev in PREP_DET:
            value *= 0.2
        if prev in PRE_VERB:
            value *= 1.5
    elif tok in ("'", "’") and prev in ELIDE:
        value = 6.0
    elif (tok == "ی" and prev == "م") or (tok == "е" and prev == "с") or (tok == "α" and prev == "ν"):
        return None, 6.0
    r = sum(w in ROMANCE_WORDS for w in words)
    e = sum(w in ENGLISH_WORDS for w in words)
    if value and not (r > e or r >= 3):
        value = 0.0
    return None, float(0.8 * value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:421, as a readable rule set.

What it does, in plain terms:

1. The first token of every document (the first token of a row, and the first
   token after each document boundary inside a packed row). This is the
   component's big spike, and its size depends on which token it is: about 3.3
   for capitalised words, about 2.9 for other words and symbols, about 2.1 for
   words that start with a space, and about 1.6 for tokens containing digits.
2. The middle-dot token "··" gives a steady +1.8.
3. Years. The second digit of "19" or "20" that begins a number pushes the
   component down: about -1.5 for "19" (as in "1995") and -1.0 for "20" (as in
   "2012"). This applies only when the "1" or "2" is not itself preceded by
   another digit, so the same pair inside a longer digit string is ignored.
4. A full stop directly after a number pushes it down: about -1.1 after a
   one-digit number ("1.", "0.") and -0.6 after a longer one ("12."). A number
   at the start of a line, or one that follows a full stop, gives nothing.
5. The ability verbs " can" (+0.3) and " could" (+0.2) give a small positive
   value. Other modals (will, would, should, may) are about zero and are left out.

Everything else is predicted as 0. The rules cover the main spikes; the many
small, unstructured values (about ±0.1) are left out.
"""

import re

READS = ()
DIGITS = set("0123456789")
MODALS = {" can": 0.3, " could": 0.2}


def first_token_value(token):
    """Size of the document-start spike for the token that starts a document."""
    if any(c in DIGITS for c in token):
        return 1.6
    if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Z][a-z]+|[A-Z]{2,}", token.strip()):
        return 3.3
    if token.startswith(" "):
        return 2.1
    return 2.9


def number_start(strings, end):
    """Index of the token just before the digit run that ends just before `end`."""
    j = end - 1
    while j >= 0 and strings[j] in DIGITS:
        j -= 1
    return j


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings
    cur = s[-1]
    # A new document starts here (or the row does): the first-token spike.
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return None, first_token_value(cur)
    if cur == "··":
        return None, 1.8
    if cur in MODALS:
        return None, MODALS[cur]
    prev = s[-2]
    before = s[-3] if len(s) > 2 else ""
    # Years: "19" or "20" beginning a number, the second digit.
    if cur in DIGITS and prev in DIGITS and before not in DIGITS:
        if prev == "1" and cur == "9":
            return None, -1.5
        if prev == "2" and cur == "0":
            return None, -1.0
    # Full stop right after a number, unless the number starts a line or follows a full stop.
    if cur == "." and prev in DIGITS:
        j = number_start(s, len(s) - 1)
        start = s[j] if j >= 0 else ""
        if start.endswith("\n") or start == ".":
            return None, 0.0
        run = len(s) - 2 - j
        return None, -1.1 if run == 1 else -0.6
    return None, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:422 — a sparse spike detector for spelling-level patterns.

This component is silent almost everywhere (it is far from zero on about 0.1% of tokens).
When it fires strongly, it does so on a few word-spelling patterns, which this program
predicts; every other token gets 0.

Positive spikes (about +3): the word "sale" and its spelling pieces, e.g. " sale",
" sales", " sal", " sil", " sail", "resale".

Negative spikes: the last letter or digit of a short capitalised or code name:
  * "x" completing a file extension or code word: ".tsx", ".jsx", "OSX" (about -8);
    a whole token "sx", "jsx", "tsx", "lsx" (about -4).
  * a digit right after a product code: "PS4", "PS3" (about -8) and "US3" (about -8);
    after other short capitalised codes (S3, TS2, NS8, ES5, RS5, ...) about -3.

The magnitudes are the group averages on training rows. The program has no state and reads
only the current token and the one before it.
"""

READS = ()

DIGITS = ("3", "4", "5", "6", "7", "8", "9")

STRONG_CODES = {"US", "PS"}                                           # digit after: about -8
WEAK_CODES = {"ES", "NS", "KS", "DS", "RS", "S", "TS", "AS", "IS"}     # digit after: about -3
X_CODES = {"js", "ts", "os", "ps", "ns", "es", "is", "us"}            # x after: about -8


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix) > 1 else ""
    core = cur.strip().lower()
    code = prev.strip().lstrip("./_")

    if core in SALE_WORDS:
        value = 3.0
    elif cur in ("x", "X") and code.lower() in X_CODES:

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection component 425, as a readable rule set.

The component is quiet on most text. It wakes up in four situations:

1. The two-dot leader token "··" (as in dotted leader lines): strongly, about 2.7.
2. Vietnamese text. "Recent Vietnamese" means a Vietnamese-only letter (đ, ơ, ư, or a
   tone-marked vowel such as ệ, ộ, ị, ủ) appeared in the last 12 tokens. There, short
   Latin pieces (1 to 4 letters) of Vietnamese words fire:
   - a bare consonant onset with no vowel yet ("Ch", "L", "g", "k", "Th"): about 2.0,
     because the syllable is unfinished;
   - a piece that contains a vowel ("can", "ập", "ị"): about 0.8;
   - other pieces (longer words, punctuation-like pieces): about 0.4.
   Romanian (which shares ă) and French/Spanish accents do not count as Vietnamese.
3. Thai-script tokens (byte-level pieces of Thai words): about 0.5.
4. The first token of each document or row, which has no context yet: about 0.3.

Everything else predicts 0. The carry is the number of tokens since the last
Vietnamese-only letter (reset at each new document).
"""

READS = ()


VIETNAMESE_ONLY = set("ạảấầẩẫậắằẳẵặẹẻẽếềểễệỉịọỏốồổỗộớờởỡợụủứừửữựỳỵỷỹđơưĐƠƯ")
VOWELS = set("aeiouyâăêôơưàáảãạèéẻẽẹìíỉĩịòóỏõọùúủũụỳýỷỹỵầấẩẫậằắẳẵặềếểễệồốổỗộờớởỡợừứửữựòó")
DOT_LEADER = "··"
THAI = ("฀", "๿")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_document = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    since = 99 if (carry is None or new_document) else carry
    since = 0 if any(c in VIETNAMESE_ONLY for c in token) else min(since + 1, 99)
    if token == DOT_LEADER:
        return since, 2.7
    if new_document:
        return since, 0.3
    if any(THAI[0] <= c <= THAI[1] for c in token):
        return since, 0.5
    piece = token.strip()
    if since <= 12 and piece.isalpha() and len(piece) <= 4:
        if any(c.lower() in VOWELS for c in piece):
            return since, 0.8
        return since, 2.0
    if since <= 12 and piece:
        return since, 0.4
    return since, 0.0

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 426.

Plain-terms summary: this component is almost always quiet (it fires on about 0.015% of
tokens). Where it does respond, it responds to two things:

1. The first token of a document. A document start that looks like code or markup
   (#include, package, //, /*, import, using, quotes, braces) pushes it negative. A start that
   looks like ordinary English prose pushes it mildly positive.
2. A few Chinese words. Work and cadre words in official prose ("工作" work, "干部" cadre,
   "活动" activity, "产业" industry) push it positive. Abstract principle nouns ("思想"
   thought, "原则" principle, "理念" ideology, "自由" freedom, "主义" -ism, "纪律" discipline,
   "方式" way/method) push it negative.

Everywhere else it predicts 0, which is its typical value.
"""

READS = ()

CODE_START = ("#", "//", "/*", "<?", '"', "{", "import", "using", "package", "def ", "int ", "require")
WORK_WORDS = {"工作", "干部", "活动", "产业", "党组织", "党建工作"}
ABSTRACT_WORDS = {"思想", "原则", "理念", "自由", "主义", "纪律", "方式", "所有", "程序", "必要", "该", "机制", "体系"}
DOC_START_CODE = -0.5
DOC_START_PROSE = 0.2
WORK_VALUE = 0.4
ABSTRACT_VALUE = -0.3


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    starts_doc = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if starts_doc:
        return None, DOC_START_CODE if token.startswith(CODE_START) else DOC_START_PROSE
    if token in WORK_WORDS:
        return None, WORK_VALUE
    if token in ABSTRACT_WORDS:
        return None, ABSTRACT_VALUE
    return None, 0.0

"""Layer 1 MLP down-projection, hidden unit 427: a weak, mostly unexplained feature
that fires on pieces of words split into several tokens, most reliably inside
German compounds built around "gegen" (entgegen, dagegen, Reparaturgegenstand).

What the program does, token by token:
  * It rebuilds the word being typed: letters since the last space or punctuation,
    lowercased, reset at each document start.
  * If that word contains "geg" (the "gegen" core), it predicts a moderately
    positive activation (+1.4) for the piece.
  * Otherwise, if the piece itself is a German "ge-" fragment ("ge", "gen", "ged",
    "geh", "gest", ...), it predicts a small positive activation (+0.4).
  * Everything else is predicted as 0.

What it leaves out: the sign of the activation is close to a coin flip for most
word pieces, and which token-level or word-level features set it is not captured
by any simple concept. A lookup table of per-token means reaches about 12% variance
explained on held-out training rows, but it is a long list of unrelated tokens
(FP, CD, GD, gcd, ...), so it is not offered here.
"""

READS = ()

GE_PIECES = {"ge", "gen", "ged", "geh", "gest", "geb", "geg"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word, last_doc = carry if carry is not None else ("", None)
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if doc != last_doc:
        word = ""
    if token[:1].isalpha():
        word += token.lower()
    elif token.startswith(" ") and token[1:2].isalpha():
        word = token[1:].lower()
    else:
        word = ""
    value = 0.0
    if "geg" in word:
        value = 1.4
    elif token in GE_PIECES:
        value = 0.4
    return (word, doc), value

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:429: a "document-start" unit.

What it does, in plain terms:
- On the first token of a document (or of a packed row), it fires strongly, about 0.4 to 1.2,
  depending on the kind of token: special markers and capitalised words fire most, punctuation
  and whitespace least. At a document start the model has no earlier context, so the value
  is set by the token alone.
- Inside a document it sits slightly below zero. The dip is deeper for longer tokens (more
  UTF-8 bytes: long word pieces dip more than one-letter pieces) and for the first few dozen
  tokens of a document, and is near zero on the token right after the start.

Mid-document values are small noise; this is the best simple description we found of their
systematic part.
"""

READS = ()


def _start_value(s):
    """Typical activation on a document's first token, from the token's decoded text."""
    if s.startswith("<|"):
        return 1.2  # special markers such as <|im_start|>
    if "�" in s:
        return 0.55  # a partial UTF-8 byte
    core = s.lstrip(" ")
    if core == "":
        return 0.43  # whitespace
    if core[0].isupper():
        return 0.75 if s.startswith(" ") else 0.9
    if core[0].isalpha() or core[0].isdigit() or ord(core[0]) > 0x3000:
        return 0.74 if s.startswith(" ") else 0.85  # lowercase words, digits, CJK
    return 0.42 if s.startswith(" ") else 0.6  # punctuation


def _inside_value(s, pos):
    """Typical activation inside a document: -0.006 per byte beyond the first, capped at -0.034,
    scaled by how far into the document the token is (pos = tokens since the document start)."""
    nbytes = len(s.encode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
    dip = -0.006 - 0.004 * min(nbytes - 1, 7)
    if pos == 1:
        return 0.2 * dip
    if pos > 100:
        return 0.6 * dip
    return dip


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    s = prefix.token_strings[t]
    starts_doc = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]
    pos = 0 if starts_doc else (carry or 0) + 1
    if starts_doc:
        value = _start_value(s)
    else:
        value = _inside_value(s, pos)
    return pos, value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:430 - the "open bracket" detector.

What it does: this component switches on at tokens that OPEN a bracketed group whose
contents continue in the same token: "(", " (", "((", "(self", "([", "('", '{"', " [",
"{", "（" and so on. Its activation is about 1.1 to 2 there and near 0 everywhere else.
Three refinements, all read off the training data:
  * bracket kind: "(" (and "（") are strongest (~1.5), "[" and "{" a bit weaker (~1.1);
  * control-flow parens ("if (", "for (", "while (", "catch (") are weak (~0.4);
  * a bracket token that also closes (")", "()", "{}") or is followed by a newline
    (" {\\n", "(\\n") does not fire.
Tokens that merely contain no opener predict 0. The program needs no state: it reads
only the newest token and the one before it.
"""

OPENERS = {"(": 1.5, "[": 1.1, "{": 1.1, "（": 1.6}   # opener -> typical activation
CLOSERS = ")]}）"
CONTROL = {"if", "for", "while", "foreach", "catch", "switch", "elif"}
READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    # A token that closes a group, or ends in whitespace/newline, does not fire.
    if any(c in CLOSERS for c in tok) or tok[-1:].isspace():
        return None, 0.0
    kinds = [OPENERS[c] for c in tok if c in OPENERS]
    if not kinds:
        return None, 0.0
    # Control-flow keyword directly before the bracket: weak.
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip() if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    if prev in CONTROL:
        return None, 0.4
    return None, kinds[0]

"""Layer-1 MLP unit 432 (down_proj): an end-of-document detector, plus a line-break term
that grows with the length of the line it ends.

What it does, in plain terms:
- The end-of-text token that closes a document: about -1.15.
- The colon of a "Title:" line that opens a document: a rare, huge negative (about -22).
- The first token of a document: mildly positive (about +0.2).
- A line break (a token containing a newline) that ends a long run of text with no
  line break in between. The longer the run, the more negative: about -0.1 after 40
  tokens, -0.3 after 80, -0.6 after 120, -0.9 after 160, -1.5 after 240. Break tokens
  that close a sentence ("." "!" "?" "。" right before the newline) get half that.
  Breaks after short lines give about zero.
- Everything else: about zero.

The carry tracks the document id, the token's index inside its document, the number of
tokens since the last line break, and the previous token, so each document starts fresh.
"""

READS = ()

END_OF_TEXT = "<|endoftext|>"
SENTENCE_END = set(".!?。")
EOT_VALUE = -1.15
TITLE_COLON_VALUE = -22.26
FIRST_TOKEN_VALUE = 0.2
# (tokens since the last line break, value of a break ending that line)
LONG_LINE_BREAKS = [(240, -1.5), (160, -0.9), (120, -0.6), (80, -0.3), (40, -0.1)]
SENTENCE_END_FACTOR = 0.5


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        index, before, since = 0, "", 0
    else:
        index, before, since = carry[1] + 1, carry[2], carry[3]
    is_break = "\n" in token
    carry = (doc, index, token, 0 if is_break else since + 1)
    if token == END_OF_TEXT:
        return carry, EOT_VALUE
    if index == 1 and before == "Title" and token == ":":
        return carry, TITLE_COLON_VALUE
    if index == 0:
        return carry, FIRST_TOKEN_VALUE
    if is_break:
        ends_sentence = token.split("\n")[0][-1:] in SENTENCE_END
        for length, value in LONG_LINE_BREAKS:
            if since >= length:
                return carry, value * (SENTENCE_END_FACTOR if ends_sentence else 1.0)
    return carry, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:433: a "p + i" spelling detector.

The component is about the letters p-i (Latin p, Greek pi, Cyrillic pe + i) inside a
word. It fires on a word piece that finishes a p-i spelling, such as "op|in" (opinion),
"lip|in", "olymp|ic", "phenotyp|ic", "nap|kin", and on whole tokens that are pic/pin
words ("pic", "pins", "pin", "topic", "epic", "-pic"). It also fires on "of" after
"top"/"bottom" ("at the top of"). It goes negative on the "p + ent / ack / enter" pieces
(pent, pack, carpenter), on the words "pent"/"penny", and on a dot-leader run "··".
Everything else is about zero. The only state is the letters of the word typed so far
in the current document.
"""
import re

READS = ()

P_STEMS = ('p', 'π', 'п')              # Latin p, Greek pi, Cyrillic pe: the stem's last letter
I_PIECES = {                           # word pieces that continue a p-i spelling: pin / pic / pik / pim
    'in', 'ino', 'inc', 'inn', 'ina', 'ic', 'ico', 'ica', 'ical', 'ically', 'ics',
    'im', 'ik', 'kin', 'ι', 'и', 'ик', 'ин',
}
PIC_PIN_TOKENS = {'pin', 'pins', 'pix', 'pinch', 'pic', 'pics', 'topic', 'topics', 'epic'}
PENT_TOKENS = {'pent', 'penny'}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    prev = '' if new_doc else (carry or '')       # letters of the word before this token
    cont = bool(tok) and not tok[0].isspace()     # continues the previous token's word
    s = tok.strip().lower()
    word = re.split(r'\W+', (prev if cont else '') + tok.lower())[-1]

    if tok == '··':                               # dot-leader run
        value = -3.5
    elif cont and prev.endswith(P_STEMS) and s in I_PIECES:
        value = 4.0                               # p | in, op | in, olymp | ic, nap | kin
    elif cont and prev in ('p', 'op') and s == 'ent':
        value = -7.0                              # p | ent (pent)
    elif cont and prev.endswith(P_STEMS) and s in ('ack', 'acker', 'enter', 'ent', 'ence', 'opt'):
        value = -4.0
    elif s.endswith('pic') and not s.endswith('scopic'):
        value = 2.5                               # topic, opic, -pic, epic
    elif s in PIC_PIN_TOKENS:
        value = 2.5                               # ' pin', ' pins', ' topic'
    elif s in PENT_TOKENS:
        value = -2.5
    elif tok == ' of' and prev.endswith(('top', 'bottom')):
        value = 3.3                               # "at the top of"
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return word, value
